reason: E4 supports laser cladding of CoCrFeNi HEAs for wear/corrosion resistance and notes their ductility. E2 supports WC as a hardness enhancer. E1 and E3 do not address the key premises: E1 discusses bulk HEA properties and E3 discusses BCC RHEAs for nuclear applications, neither supporting the specific CoCrFeNi-WC composite, crack inhibition mechanism, or hot cracking reduction.
premises: Laser cladding can deposit CoCrFeNi-based HEA coatings with refined microstructures and metallurgical bonding.
Adding WC particles to a metallic matrix improves hardness and wear resistance.
CoCrFeNi-based HEAs possess good ductility and corrosion resistance.
Rapid solidification and grain refinement reduce hot cracking tendency.
